dedupe_keys.name: qposd gulf of mexico quad polarization sar oil spill masks

description: The QPOSD authors assembled 41 fully polarimetric L-band NASA/JPL UAVSAR scenes over the U.S. Gulf of Mexico from 2010 to 2022. Each scene uses HH, HV, VH and VV channels and pixel-level masks distinguishing sea surface, oil spills, look-alike phenomena and land. The article reports multi-look SAR scenes at roughly 6-by-4-metre resolution and varying incidence angles. The current Zenodo version lists a nearly 3.9 GB ZIP archive and two Python loading or patch examples. It is open under CC BY 4.0, with free access. Coverage is selected Gulf scenes, not all offshore spills or a real-time monitoring service. Normalized imagery, class annotation and look-alike conditions limit transfer to other sensors and coasts; no pixel labels or model scores were checked. A reviewer-assessed simulation use is testing marine spill exposure or response-detection components near shipping and oil infrastructure. data-iceye-open-sar-data is a related SAR source, without harmonized acquisition settings. No ZIP, script or article PDF was downloaded.
